location_note: Eastern slope of Mount Scopus below Augusta Victoria Hospital, south-west bank of Wadi Abu Harub; map ref. 22390-415/63300-315 (NIG, preliminary-excavation permit note). The converted point lies in Z4 near its eastern limit.
notes: Final report of the chalk quarry and vessel-production cave complex (1st c. CE, perhaps to 132-135 CE) and the adjacent limestone quarry (Segments I-VI) with earlier installations: Iron II winepress and southern pool; eastern pool (Iron II or Early Roman); Early Roman stepped cistern L1560, cist graves and kokhim cave T44; tunnel T45 undated; quarry Late Roman-Byzantine. Ras Tumeim cisterns, columbarium and other caves are cited from earlier work; not coded. The geology report is ATQ113-i11.

features.subtype: artificial chalk quarry and chalk-vessel production cave complex (lower and upper caves, courtyard)
features.period: 1st c. CE (pottery, coins to 69 CE); possible activity until the Bar Kokhba Revolt
features.quote: dated by pottery and coins to the first century CE
